title: Pressure in solids
examples: Teacher, how does the size of the object change the pressure?
Can you show me an example where pressure is important in everyday life?
What is the difference between force and pressure?

explain.say: Pressure is a measure of force spread over an area.
The formula we use is pressure equals force divided by area.
If you increase the force, the pressure also increases.
If you decrease the area, the pressure will increase for the same force.
Snowshoes spread your weight over a large area to reduce pressure.
Knives have sharp edges to concentrate the force onto a small area.

faq.q: What is the unit for pressure?
faq.a: The standard unit for pressure is Pascals, which is Newtons per square meter.
asks: What are the units of pressure?

faq.q: Does the force have to be a weight?
faq.a: No, the force can be any push or pull, not just the weight of an object.
asks: Is weight the only force I can use?

faq.q: If I double the area, what happens to the pressure?
faq.a: If you double the area, the pressure will be cut in half, assuming the force stays the same.
asks: If A doubles, what happens to P?

faq.q: Does the material matter for pressure?
faq.a: The material itself does not change the calculation of pressure, only the force and area do.
asks: Does the type of solid matter?
Is it about the material or the size?

faq.q: Can I use this idea for liquids too?
faq.a: This concept extends to liquids, but the pressure calculation involves depth as well.

facts: Pressure is calculated by dividing the force by the area.
The unit for pressure is the Pascal, or Newtons per square meter.
Increasing the area decreases the pressure for a constant force.
Sharper objects concentrate force onto a very small area.

quiz.say: A box exerts a force of 50 Newtons over an area of 2 square meters. What is the pressure?
quiz.why: You divide the force by the area, so 50 divided by 2 is 25.

wrong.0: You multiplied the force by the area, which is incorrect for pressure.
wrong.1: You subtracted the area from the force, which does not relate to pressure.
wrong.2: You divided the force by 10 times the area, which is an extra step.

quiz.say: To reduce the pressure from your weight on snow, what should you do?
quiz.why: Snowshoes increase the area, which lowers the pressure from your weight.

wrong.0: Jumping harder increases the force, which would increase the pressure.
wrong.1: Standing on your toes decreases the area, which increases the pressure.
wrong.2: Walking faster does not change the area or the force applied to the snow.

quiz.say: A sharp knife blade and a blunt block both have the same force applied. Which has higher pressure?
quiz.why: The sharp knife blade has a much smaller area, making the pressure much higher.

wrong.0: The blunt block has a larger area, which spreads the force out and lowers the pressure.
wrong.1: Pressure depends on the area, so the smaller area makes the pressure higher.
wrong.2: The question states the force is the same for both objects.
